```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(pROC)
library(caret)
```


### DATA CLEANING
```{r}
# load dataset
data = read.csv("D:/WORK/PROJECT/Churn/WA_Fn-UseC_-Telco-Customer-Churn(3).csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
str(data)
dim(data)

# missing values, duplicate
colSums(is.na(data))
sum(duplicated(data))
sum(duplicated(data$customerID))

# records with missing TotalCharges
data[is.na(data$TotalCharges),c("customerID", "tenure", "MonthlyCharges","TotalCharges", "Churn")]

# remove records
data_clean = data[!is.na(data$TotalCharges), ]

# categorical -> factors
categorical_vars = c("gender", "SeniorCitizen", "Partner", "Dependents","PhoneService","InternetService", "Contract", "PaperlessBilling", "PaymentMethod")

data_clean[categorical_vars] = lapply(
  data_clean[categorical_vars],factor)

# final dataset
dim(data_clean)
colSums(is.na(data_clean))
str(data_clean)
```

### EDA

```{r}
# churn distribution
table(data_clean$Churn)

# churn proportion
round(prop.table(table(data_clean$Churn)) * 100, 2)
```
```{r}
# churn rate
churn_rates = map_dfr(categorical_vars, function(var) {
  data_clean %>%
    group_by(category = .data[[var]]) %>%
    summarise(
      total = n(),
      churn_rate = mean(Churn == "Yes") * 100,
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(variable = var, .before = 1)})

churn_rates %>%
  mutate(churn_rate = round(churn_rate, 2))
```

### BIVARIATE

```{r}
# chi-square tests (categorical predictors)

chi_square_results = lapply(categorical_vars, function(var) {
  tab = table(data_clean[[var]], data_clean$Churn)
  test = chisq.test(tab)

  data.frame(
    variable = var,
    chi_square = unname(test$statistic),
    df = unname(test$parameter),
    p_value = test$p.value)})

chi_square_results = do.call(rbind, chi_square_results)

chi_square_results$p_value = signif(
  chi_square_results$p_value, 5)

chi_square_results[
  order(chi_square_results$p_value),]

```

```{r}
# wilcoxon rank-sum tests (numerical predictors)

numerical_vars = c("tenure", "MonthlyCharges", "TotalCharges")

wilcoxon_results = lapply(numerical_vars, function(var) {
  test = wilcox.test(
    data_clean[[var]] ~ data_clean$Churn,
    exact = FALSE)

  data.frame(
    variable = var,
    wilcoxon_statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value)})

wilcoxon_results = do.call(rbind, wilcoxon_results)

wilcoxon_results$p_value = signif(
  wilcoxon_results$p_value, 4)

wilcoxon_results
```

```{r}
# association strength using Cramer's V

cramers_v_results = lapply(categorical_vars, function(var) {
  tab = table(data_clean[[var]], data_clean$Churn)
  test = chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)

  n = sum(tab)
  r = nrow(tab)
  k = ncol(tab)

  v = sqrt(
    unname(test$statistic) /
      (n * min(r - 1, k - 1)))

  data.frame(
    variable = var,
    cramers_v = v)})

cramers_v_results = do.call(rbind, cramers_v_results)

cramers_v_results = cramers_v_results[
  order(-cramers_v_results$cramers_v),]

cramers_v_results$cramers_v = round(
  cramers_v_results$cramers_v, 3)

cramers_v_results
```


### LOGISTIC REGRESSION

```{r}
# set reference category for the response variable
data_clean$Churn = relevel(
  data_clean$Churn,
  ref = "No")

levels(data_clean$Churn)

# fit the model
model_initial = glm(Churn ~ SeniorCitizen + gender + PhoneService + Partner + Dependents + tenure + TotalCharges + MonthlyCharges + InternetService + Contract + PaperlessBilling + PaymentMethod, data = data_clean, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(model_initial)
```

### MODEL DIAGNOSTIC

```{r}
# linearity in the logit
model_nonlinear = update(
  model_initial,
  . ~ . +
    I(tenure^2) +
    I(TotalCharges^2) +
    I(MonthlyCharges^2))

anova(model_initial, model_nonlinear, test = "Chisq")

summary(model_nonlinear)
```
```{r}
# influential observation
plot(model_initial, which = 4)
```
```{r}
# multicolinearity
vif(model_initial)
```

### EVALUATION

```{r}
# churn prob
prob_initial = predict(
  model_initial,
  type = "response")

pred_initial = ifelse(
  prob_initial >= 0.5,
  "Yes", "No")

conf_initial = table(
  Actual = data_clean$Churn,
  Predicted = factor(
    pred_initial,
    levels = c("No", "Yes")))

conf_initial

TN = conf_initial["No", "No"]
FP = conf_initial["No", "Yes"]
FN = conf_initial["Yes", "No"]
TP = conf_initial["Yes", "Yes"]

accuracy = (TP + TN) / sum(conf_initial)
sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN)
specificity = TN / (TN + FP)
precision = TP / (TP + FP)

c(Accuracy = accuracy,
  Sensitivity = sensitivity,
  Specificity = specificity,
  Precision = precision)
```
```{r}
# ROC
roc_initial = roc(
  response = data_clean$Churn,
  predictor = prob_initial,
  levels = c("No", "Yes"),
  direction = "<")

auc(roc_initial)
```
### TRAIN-TEST

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

train_index = sample(
  seq_len(nrow(data_clean)),
  size = floor(0.8 * nrow(data_clean)))

train_data = data_clean[train_index, ]
test_data  = data_clean[-train_index, ]

nrow(train_data)
nrow(test_data)

model_train = glm(Churn ~ SeniorCitizen + gender + PhoneService + Partner + Dependents + tenure + TotalCharges + MonthlyCharges + InternetService + Contract + PaperlessBilling + PaymentMethod, data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(model_train)
```

```{r}
# odds ratios
or_data = broom::tidy(
  model_train,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Predictor = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      "SeniorCitizen1" = "Senior Citizen: Yes",
      "genderMale" = "Gender: Male",
      "PhoneServiceYes" = "Phone Service: Yes",
      "PartnerYes" = "Partner: Yes",
      "DependentsYes" = "Dependents: Yes",
      "tenure" = "Tenure",
      "TotalCharges" = "Total Charges",
      "MonthlyCharges" = "Monthly Charges",
      "InternetServiceFiber optic" = "Internet: Fiber Optic",
      "InternetServiceNo" = "Internet: No Service",
      "ContractOne year" = "Contract: One Year",
      "ContractTwo year" = "Contract: Two Year",
      "PaperlessBillingYes" = "Paperless Billing: Yes",
      "PaymentMethodCredit card (automatic)" =
        "Payment: Credit Card (Automatic)",
      "PaymentMethodElectronic check" =
        "Payment: Electronic Check",
      "PaymentMethodMailed check" = "Payment: Mailed Check"))

# order predictors for plotting
or_data$Predictor = factor(
  or_data$Predictor,
  levels = rev(c(
    "Senior Citizen: Yes",
    "Gender: Male",
    "Phone Service: Yes",
    "Partner: Yes",
    "Dependents: Yes",
    "Tenure",
    "Total Charges",
    "Monthly Charges",
    "Internet: Fiber Optic",
    "Internet: No Service",
    "Contract: One Year",
    "Contract: Two Year",
    "Paperless Billing: Yes",
    "Payment: Credit Card (Automatic)",
    "Payment: Electronic Check",
    "Payment: Mailed Check")))

# forest Plot
ggplot(or_data, aes(x = estimate, y = Predictor)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
    orientation = "y",
    width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "#2878B5") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Odds Ratios of Customer Churn Predictors",
    subtitle = "Training Model | 95% Confidence Intervals",
    x = "Odds Ratio (log scale)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Reference line at OR = 1.",
      "Intervals crossing 1 indicate no statistical significance",
      "at the 5% level using Wald confidence intervals.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

### EVALUATION (TRAIN_TEST)

```{r}
# churn prob
test_prob = predict(
  model_train,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response")

test_pred = ifelse(
  test_prob >= 0.5,
  "Yes", "No")

# conf matrix
conf_test = table(
  Actual = test_data$Churn,
  Predicted = factor(
    test_pred,
    levels = c("No", "Yes")))

conf_test

TN = conf_test["No", "No"]
FP = conf_test["No", "Yes"]
FN = conf_test["Yes", "No"]
TP = conf_test["Yes", "Yes"]

accuracy = (TP + TN) / sum(conf_test)
sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN)
specificity = TN / (TN + FP)
precision = TP / (TP + FP)

c(Accuracy = accuracy,
  Sensitivity = sensitivity,
  Specificity = specificity,
  Precision = precision)

```

```{r}
# heatmap
cm_df = as.data.frame(conf_test)

ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#DCEAF7", high = "#372776") +
  labs(
    title = "Confusion Matrix",
    subtitle = "Test Set | Classification Threshold = 0.5",
    x = "Predicted Class",
    y = "Actual Class",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r}
# ROC
roc_test = roc(
  response = test_data$Churn,
  predictor = test_prob,
  levels = c("No", "Yes"),
  direction = "<")

auc(roc_test)

plot(
  roc_test,
  print.auc = TRUE,
  main = "ROC Curve - Initial Logistic Regression Model")
```
